title: Force on moving charges; Magnetic fields and field patterns; Fields of currents (quantitative); Charged particles in uniform electric fields
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for Eduqas A-level Physics (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: MG01-1#t3 term and clue written for the game; MG01-1#t4 term and clue written for the game; MG01-1#t1 term and clue written for the game; MG01-1#t2 term and clue written for the game. Questions: F05-1#N.3, MG01-1#N.5, MG03-1#N.3b, MG04-1#N.3, F05-1#N.5a, MG01-1#N.7, MG03-1#N.6a, MG04-1#N.9, F05-1#N.8a, MG03-1#N.17, MG04-1#N.12a, F05-1#N.14.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Solenoid
items.clue: Long coil whose inside pattern is straight, parallel and evenly spaced.

items.label: Compass needle
items.clue: Pointer whose north end shows which way the pattern runs at that place.

items.label: Magnetic field
items.clue: Region produced by moving charges that pushes on currents and on iron or steel.

items.label: Field lines
items.clue: Closed loops, never crossing, drawn closer together where the effect is stronger.

questions.stem: Two horizontal parallel plates, 2.5 cm apart in a vacuum, have a potential difference of 150 V between them. What is the magnitude of the acceleration of an electron between the plates? Gravity is negligible. Take e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C and m_e = 9.11 × 10⁻³¹ kg.

options.text: 1.1 × 10¹³ m s⁻²
2.6 × 10¹³ m s⁻²
6.6 × 10¹¹ m s⁻²
1.1 × 10¹⁵ m s⁻²

questions.stem: A long, straight, vertical wire carries a steady current upwards. Point P is 5.0 cm due east of the wire, level with it. What is the direction of the magnetic field of the wire at P?

options.text: Due south, at a tangent to a circle around the wire
Due east, directly away from the wire along a radius
Due north, at a tangent to a circle centred on the wire
Vertically upwards, parallel to the direction of the current

questions.explanation: Right thumb up, along the current: the fingers curl around the wire, and on its east side they point due north. The field is a tangent to a circle centred on the wire.

questions.stem: An electron moves towards the right of the page, in the plane of the page, through a uniform magnetic field directed into the page. What is the direction of the magnetic force on the electron at that instant?

options.text: Towards the top of the page
Towards the bottom of the page
Towards the left of the page
Into the plane of the page

questions.stem: A long straight wire of diameter 0.010 m carries a current of 12 A. Point P is 0.045 m from the surface of the wire. What is the magnitude of the magnetic field produced by the wire at P? (Use μ₀ = 4π × 10⁻⁷ T m A⁻¹.)

Two parallel plates, 2.0 cm apart in a vacuum, have a potential difference of 500 V between them. An electron is released from rest at the negative plate and accelerates across the gap. What is its speed when it reaches the positive plate? Take e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C and m_e = 9.11 × 10⁻³¹ kg.
You look at the left end of a long solenoid. Seen from there, the current in its turns flows clockwise. Which end of the solenoid is its north end?

options.text: The left end, the one you are looking at
The right end, the far end from you
Neither: inside, the field is uniform, so there are no poles
It depends on the size of the current in the turns

questions.explanation: Fingers clockwise as seen from the left, so the thumb points to the right. Inside, the field runs left to right and leaves through the right end. Field lines leave a north end, so that end is N.

questions.stem: A proton moves in a circle in a uniform magnetic field that is perpendicular to its velocity. A second proton moves at twice the speed of the first, perpendicular to the same field. Compared with the first proton, what are the radius of the second proton's circle and the time it takes to complete one revolution?

options.text: Radius halved; time for one revolution reduced to a quarter
Radius doubled; time for one revolution unchanged
Radius unchanged; time for one revolution halved
Radius doubled; time for one revolution halved as well

questions.stem: A long solenoid with N turns and length L has a field of magnitude B₀ inside it when the current is I. A second long solenoid has the same number of turns N spread over a length 2L and twice the radius, and it carries the same current I. What is the magnitude of the field inside the second solenoid?

An electron moves horizontally into the region between two horizontal parallel plates, midway between them and at right angles to the uniform electric field between the plates. It is deflected towards the positive plate. Gravity is negligible. Which describes the motion of the electron while it is between the plates?

options.text: A parabola: its horizontal velocity is constant as it accelerates towards the positive plate
A circular arc at constant speed, with the force at right angles to its velocity
A straight line at an angle, moving towards the positive plate at a steady velocity
A curve along which its horizontal velocity decreases as it is pulled sideways

questions.stem: Two protons enter two separate regions at the same speed. Region 1 contains only a uniform electric field; region 2 contains only a uniform magnetic field. Each proton enters at right angles to the field lines. Gravity is negligible. A short time later, which statement is correct?

options.text: Both protons still have their starting speed, because each force began at right angles to the motion.
Only the proton in the magnetic field still has its starting speed.
Only the proton in the electric field still has its starting speed.
Both protons have sped up, because each one is pushed by a force.

questions.stem: Two long straight parallel wires in air are 4.0 cm apart and carry currents of 5.0 A and 8.0 A. What is the magnitude of the magnetic force on a 1.5 m length of the wire carrying 8.0 A? Take μ₀ = 4π × 10⁻⁷ T m A⁻¹ for air.

A proton and an alpha particle are placed, one at a time, at the same point in a uniform electric field. The alpha particle has twice the charge of the proton and about four times its mass. Gravity is negligible. What is the ratio (acceleration of the alpha particle) / (acceleration of the proton)?
questions.explanation: Correct. Acceleration = charge × E ÷ mass, so the ratio is (2/4) = 1/2. The alpha particle accelerates half as much.
